parsed.why: New criminal statute threatens imprisonment/deportation, but no documented trans targeting; military hostility and absent protections keep it high-risk, not near-certain execution.
Decriminalised conduct and no trans-specific law, but unenforced entry ban, no SOGI recourse, and dating-app ambushes show private violence rather than state execution.
Strong legal protections and courts, but patterned lethal attacks and kill-lists against trans people; state accountability improves but does not reach reduced risk.
Documented police harassment, arbitrary arrests and violent detention of transgender people outweigh the absence of criminalisation; little protection for visitors.
Constitutional equality, hate-crime law and binding court relief protect, but ID mismatch, facility ambiguity and township violence keep it below low risk.
